requirement.evidence: In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%. The allowable annual increase will not be permitted, if the dwelling is not in substantial compliance and/or if the landlord has not met the registration requirements as specified in this subsection 19:2-9.8.
requirement.note: The 12-month period and the "irrespective of ... change of ownership" language appear in the page text. The advice to check registration is a practical addition, not a legal claim.

key_value.evidence: The rents for any housing space shall not be increased more than the percentages stated below in any consecutive 12-month period, irrespective of the number of different tenants occupying the housing space during the 12-month period, any change of ownership of the Landlord or vacancy of the housing space.
key_value.note: The 4% cap applies per 12-month period. The cap is stated in the 19:2-3.1 text.

effective_date.note: The ordinance citation date and the statement that the ordinance was amended on September 05, 2017 support the date. The page does not say explicitly that the 4% cap took effect on that date.

status.evidence: Pursuant to 19:2-3. Rent Increases. 19:2-3.1. Determination of Rents. In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%.
status.note: The page presents the cap as current law. The 2020 moratorium was rescinded on September 18, 2023, so it does not suspend the cap as of 2026-10-01.

coverage.note: The coverage field is empty on the card.
